[[No overall control]]{{efn|Labour minority.}} | after_election = | after_party = }} {{Main|Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council elections}} The '''2026 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026, alongside the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections across the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day, to elect 19 of 38 members of [[Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council]] in [[Warwickshire]], [[England]].{{Cite web|title=The one political group which wants Nuneaton and Bedworth elections delayed|url=https://www.coventrytelegraph.net/news/local-news/one-political-party-wants-2026-33173044|website=Coventry Live|date=2026-01-06|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en|first=Claire|last=Harrison}} Due to ongoing [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisation]], this will be the final election to Nuneaton & Bedworth Borough Council before it is abolished and replaced by a successor [[unitary authority]]. Elections to the successor authority are due to take place in 2027. ==Summary== ===Background=== In [[2024 Nuneaton and Bedworth Borough Council election|2024]], the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] lost control of the council to the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]].{{Cite news|title=Nuneaton & Bedworth result - Local Elections 2024|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000219|work=BBC News|access-date=2026-01-30|language=en-GB}} Due to ongoing [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisation]], the Local Government Secretary, Steve Reed, wrote to all local authorities due to have elections in 2026, asking if they would like to delay their elections to 2027.{{Cite web|first=Jennifer |last=McKiernan |author-link= |first2=Alex |last2=Forsyth |author2-link= |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2ggk333l4o |website=bbc.com |title=Thirty English councils to delay elections, minister confirms |pages= |date=29 January 2026 |access-date=6 February 2026 |work= |publisher=[[BBC News]] |place= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260206113227/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2ggk333l4o |archive-date=6 February 2026 }} The council's Labour group supported delaying the election, while the opposition parties were against the plans. Watkins said, "it was felt that holding [the election] for a local authority that is shortly to be abolished is not a prudent use of resources".{{Cite web|first=Simon |last=Gilbert |author-link= |first2= |last2= |author2-link= |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c24gg35l0leo |website=bbc.com |title=Council leader ousted over election delay row |pages= |date=22 January 2026 |access-date=5 February 2026 |work= |publisher=[[BBC News]] |place= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260123051600/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c24gg35l0leo |archive-date=23 January 2026 }} Following this, an extraordinary general meeting of the council was called, and a motion of [[no confidence]] in the council leader was moved by Conservative leader Kris Wilson (Whitestone). The motion passed with the support of the Conservative, Green, and Liberal Democrat councillors, and Watkins was removed from the position. Labour councillor Steve Hey (Attleborough) was subsequently selected to replace Watkins as leader.
